description: Primary-source review for the Lorenz demo. Brunton 2016 (recovers) and Kaheman 2020 (original SINDy fails) form a candidate pair whose deciding condition is noise placement, but unstated thresholds keep it out of exact reproduction. See docs/real-pair-review.md. Keep synthetic scenarios separate.

sources.title: Discovering governing equations from data: Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamical systems
sources.quote: to investigate the effect of noisy derivatives.
sources.outcome_summary: Table 4 reports the correct Lorenz terms at derivative-noise variance 1; the text says the form of the equations holds up to variance 10. With threshold 0.025, exact derivatives and plain least squares the adapter reproduces this (coefficient error 0.0002), but those three settings are not stated in the paper.
blockers: The threshold is not stated; 0.025 comes from the authors' released code, not the paper.
The text describes convex l1 minimisation; Code 1 uses sequentially thresholded least squares without a ridge penalty. The adapter reproduces Table 4 only with ridge 0.
Whether the clean derivatives are exact or numerical is not stated.
Table 4 reports coefficients from a single noise realisation, not an aggregate measurement.

sources.outcome_summary: The study compares smoothers with STLS and WBPDN. Its explicit Table 2 forecast numbers use l1-trend filtering and WBPDN, which the current adapter does not support.
blockers: The exact smoother and parameter-selection procedure are not represented by a generic smoothed-sindy label.
Table 2 values belong to unsupported WBPDN, not the adapter's STLS.
STLS coefficient-error figures require careful scalar extraction; unstable forecast realizations were excluded from some aggregation.

sources.title: Automatic Differentiation to Simultaneously Identify Nonlinear Dynamics and Extract Noise Probability Distributions from Data
sources.locator: Appendix E and Figure 14 (PDF pages 24-25); Section 3.2 and Eq. 19 (PDF page 7); Section 4.4 (PDF page 13)
sources.quote: 5 different noisy data sets are generated and provided to both approaches.

stated_conditions.noise_definition: Eq. 19: noise level (%) = var(noise) / var(signal) x 100
stated_conditions.threshold_sweep: 100 uniform values from 0.01 to the smallest true coefficient magnitude

sources.outcome_summary: Figure 14's bar labels give 8% as the most noise original SINDy handles on Lorenz (18% with smoothing). Read as Eq. 19's variance ratio, the adapter recovers all five datasets only up to 0.25% and none from 1%; read as a standard-deviation ratio, all five recover at 6% and none from 10% (scripts/real_pair_probe.py).
blockers: The 8% limit is read from figure bar labels, not stated in prose.
The rule for picking a threshold from the sweep is not stated.
The finite-difference scheme and the original SINDy library are not stated.
Eq. 19 defines noise by variance ratio, Section 4.4 multiplies noise by percentage x var(signal), and only a standard-deviation ratio reproduces the 8% limit.
Whether the signal variance is per state or pooled, and which noise levels were tested, is not stated.
